period_mismatch_note: Period mismatch: this report covers 31 days (Aug 14 – Sep 13) but the prior report covered a 15-day fortnight (Jul 30 – Aug 13). Raw volume deltas — spend, leads, conversions, calls, sessions, impressions — are inflated roughly 2× by the longer window and should not be read as growth. Rate metrics (cost per lead, cost per click, click-through rate, conversion rate, answer rate, search position, pages per user) compare cleanly. Per-day normalization: spend per day $613 → $663 (+8%), leads per day 3.0 → 3.42 (+14%), calls per day 0.40 → 0.84 (+110%). Note that Looker's built-in Google Analytics and Search Console comparisons ARE like-for-like (this 31-day window vs the preceding 31 days, Jul 14 – Aug 13), so the website and organic growth percentages in this report are clean.
cadence_note: The regular 30-day report cadence resumes with this edition after a run of fortnight snapshots (Jul 14, Jul 27, Jul 30 and Aug 13). Because the immediately preceding edition was a 15-day window, see period_mismatch_note before reading any raw volume delta.

summary.narrative: This was the strongest month on record for lead volume: 106 paid leads on $20.6K of spend, and a blended cost per lead of $194 — the lowest reading yet, edging past the $204 posted last fortnight even as the window doubled in length. Meta did the heavy lifting with 64 leads at $136.19 each, led by Remarketing at $46.85 and Brochure Download at $87.05. Google delivered 42 conversions at $282, and the two campaigns that spent $2,124 with nothing to show last period — Search_Competitors and Key Feeder Markets — are now converting, at 5 and 5.5 respectively; Display added 14 conversions at $110.88, though most of its phone leads were anonymous callers. The site itself was flat: Looker's like-for-like read puts active users at +0.7% and views at −2.7%. Search impressions grew 23.2%, but average position slipped from 14.7 to 16.0, largely on wrong-city Miramar, Florida apartment queries that earn impressions and no clicks. The phone is the caveat that persists. 26 calls came in and 14 were answered — a 54% answer rate, up from 33% but still under the 70% floor — with 12 missed and none tagged as leads. Pipeline is moving the right way: the warm bench grew from 7 to 19, sales visits doubled from 4 to 8, reservations held at 2, and there are still zero hot leads. Two new channels also appeared this period — a Wall Street Journal preseason-2026 placement drove 1,267 sessions and wfla CTV/addressable display in New York drove 207 — but neither has cost or conversion data in the dashboard yet. Cheap leads are arriving in volume; the job now is answering the phone and converting the bench.

website_organic.looker_reported_deltas_note: Unlike previous editions, which computed growth against the values published in the prior report, THIS period's growth percentages use Looker's own built-in comparison against the preceding 31 days (Jul 14 – Aug 13). The prior report was a 15-day window, so a direct comparison to its published values (3.7K users, 6.4K views, 4.8K impressions, 211 queries) would show roughly doubled figures that reflect the window length, not real growth. Looker's like-for-like reading: active users +0.7%, new users −0.2%, views −2.7%, pages per user −3.4%, search position +14.0% (worse), impressions +23.2%, queries +2.1%.
website_organic.traffic_quality_note: Traffic is flat on a like-for-like basis: 10.1K active users (+0.7%), 17.6K views (−2.7%) and 1.7 pages per user (−3.4%). Paid channels supply two-thirds of visits — paid social 33.3% and paid search 31.7% — with direct at 22.2% and organic search at 6.3%. Google sessions totaled 4,635 (1,950 of them from Display placements) and Meta 2,160. Desktop visitors stay longest at 2:02 average session duration versus 1:27 on mobile and tablet.
website_organic.position_note: Average organic position worsened from 14.7 to 16.0 while impressions rose 23.2% to 13.9K and queries edged up 2.1% to 336. The impression growth is largely hollow: at least 1,656 impressions in the visible top-26 terms came from Miramar, Florida apartment and property-management searches with zero clicks. Branded searches remain solid — 'mira mar sarasota' alone drew 2,252 impressions and 43 clicks, and the four branded variants together 4,268 impressions and 113 clicks.
website_organic.engagement_highlight: The deep-intent pages continue to hold visitors: the Broker Toolkit averaged 3:17 per visit, Our History 2:41, Team 2:11, and the Residences page combined a 7.99% bounce rate with 2:04 on page. The Contact page's bounce rate rose to 37.55% (from 4.11% last period) at 44 seconds, worth watching. Brochure Download (56.88%, 26 seconds) and Reserve (60.3%) are single-purpose pages where a high bounce is expected.
website_organic.wrong_city_note: At least 1,656 impressions in the visible top-26 search terms came from Miramar, Florida apartment, rental and property-management searches (11 distinct queries), every one with zero clicks. The true total is higher — 336 queries exist and only the top 26 were captured. This is the main reason average position worsened to 16.0 and accounts for much of the 23.2% impression growth.
website_organic.new_channels_note: Two channels appeared for the first time this period: a Wall Street Journal 'preseason-2026' placement delivered 1,267 sessions (the third-largest source, behind only Google and Meta), and wfla CTV / addressable display targeting New York delivered 207 sessions (122 addressable display, 85 CTV). chatgpt.com also referred 18 sessions as an AI-assistant source. None of the three carry cost or conversion data in the dashboard.

recommendations.headline: Phone coverage is better but still under the 70% floor — assign a callback owner
recommendations.detail: The answer rate recovered from 33% to 54%: 26 calls came in, 14 were answered, 12 were missed and none of the 26 was tagged as a lead. Google Ads drove 16 of those calls, so every missed one was paid for. Reinstating the backup ring group got half the way there; the remaining gap needs a named owner for same-day callback on every missed number and a check that the 14 zero-call days are genuinely quiet rather than a routing problem.

recommendations.headline: Fund Meta Remarketing and Brochure Download further; watch Feeder Market Segmented
recommendations.detail: Remarketing produced 13 leads at $46.85 and Brochure Download 18 at $87.05 — together 31 leads on $2,176, the cheapest leads in the account. Feeder Market Segmented took the largest Meta budget ($4,077) and returned 16 leads at $254.83, well above the $150 target. Shift budget from Segmented into Remarketing and Brochure Download, and give the two New LP landing-page tests (5 leads at $154.66 and 1 at $145.45) another period before judging them.

recommendations.headline: Google: Competitors and Key Feeder Markets are converting again — keep them, but cap them
recommendations.detail: After spending $2,124 with zero conversions last period, Search_Competitors delivered 5 conversions and Key Feeder Markets 5.5 this period. The expensive half of the account is now Non-Brand Sarasota at $443.83 per lead on $5,992 and Competitors at $463.13 on $2,316 — both well above the $282 account blend and Branded at $115.48. Keep Competitors and Key Feeder live now that they convert, but hold their budgets flat and push Non-Brand Sarasota's bid strategy toward its 16 form submissions rather than click volume.

recommendations.headline: Judge Display on form fills, not its $110.88 cost per lead
recommendations.detail: Display posted 14 conversions at $110.88 on 791.7K impressions, the best-looking Google line on paper. But 12 of Google's 17 phone-call leads came from Display and most were anonymous 'Wireless Caller' entries; only 7 of the 17 have a recorded duration and 3 lasted over two minutes. Display's 4 form submissions are the firmer signal. Keep it at the current scale for reach, and track it on form submissions and Spark-rated leads going forward.

recommendations.headline: Organic position slipped to 16.0 — the Miramar, FL problem is growing with impressions
recommendations.detail: Search impressions grew 23.2% like-for-like to 13.9K, but average position worsened from 14.7 to 16.0 for the second consecutive report. At least 1,656 impressions in the visible top terms came from Miramar, Florida apartment, rental and property-management searches with zero clicks — up from 237 last period. Add explicit 'Sarasota' geographic disambiguation to title tags and structured data, keep publishing Sarasota-anchored content, and consider whether the wrong-city queries can be discouraged through page copy rather than left to dilute position.

recommendations.headline: WSJ, wfla and Microsoft/Bing are driving sessions with no cost data — get the spend into the dashboard
recommendations.detail: Three channels delivered 2,694 sessions this period without a cost or conversion figure anywhere in the dashboard: the Wall Street Journal preseason-2026 placement (1,267 sessions, the third-largest source), Microsoft paid search (1,220 — now open for three reports) and wfla CTV / addressable display in New York (207). Confirm the spend on each with the client and add the sources so their true cost per lead can sit alongside Google's $282 and Meta's $136.

recommendations.headline: The warm bench grew to 19 and sales visits doubled to 8 — work it before buying more volume
recommendations.detail: The warm bench nearly tripled from 7 to 19, sales visits or meetings doubled from 4 to 8, reservations held at 2, and there are still zero hot leads. Seven new warm prospects arrived in the period — Daniel Herscovici is visiting and wants to see the location, Stephen Heffron asked about process and timeline — alongside long-lead prospects Fanny Lange ($5–7M, possible visit this month), Walter Cleary (around $6M) and Steve Shuhet ($3–5M, fall visit). With cost per lead at its best on record, the constraint on reservations is follow-up capacity, not lead supply.
